brief: A meeting scheduler where time flows as a river — free slots are calm water, meetings are bridges

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: bridges-over-river maps meetings vs free time into an immediately legible visual story
The 'NOW' marker as a vertical light beam is genuinely poetic and anchors the timeline with emotional clarity
Distinctive 3D perspective gives the schedule a memorable, sculptural identity rare in calendar UIs
dominant_weaknesses: Free-slot pills are clipped and overlapped by bridge cards, making available times nearly unreadable — core function broken
Time labels float disconnected above the scene with no clear alignment to bridges, so scanning a meeting's hour requires guesswork
Muddy olive/brown banks clash with the cool blue water and dusty-purple bridges, producing a murky, unresolved palette
fix_priorities: Fix occlusion: stagger or elevate free-slot pills above bridges so availability is never hidden
Tie time ruler to bridge positions with vertical guides or anchored labels for unambiguous time reading
Re-tune palette — desaturate banks or shift to a cohesive analogous scheme so water, bridges, and shore harmonize
Reduce perspective distortion or offer a flatter mode for dense days where 3D becomes a usability tax
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral metaphor and reflective charm carry the design while behavioral usability collapses under occluded slots and unanchored time labels.
rationale.intent_fit: The river/bridge metaphor is executed literally and evocatively, but the poetic framing actively obstructs the scheduling task it's meant to serve.
